plan.notes: Source: official UNM Catalog page 'Undergraduate Program — Computer Science', http://catalog.unm.edu/catalogs/2021-2022/colleges/engineering/computer-science/undergraduate-program.html (UNM 2021-2022 Catalog). Transcription: manual transcription of the catalog's official model schedule ('Bachelor of Science in Computer Science' — the catalog's term-by-term planning guide) on 2026-09-30; course titles copied as printed in the catalog. Catalog year is 2021-2022 because the current (2026-2027) catalog's Computer Science program page could not be fetched (upstream access failure); re-verify against the current catalog before release. Official degree name per catalog: 'Bachelor of Science in Computer Science' (B.S.C.S.); 120 total credit hours. The catalog states the schedule is a guide and must be adjusted for deficiencies/advanced preparation: ACT/SAT placement governs math and English entry, and students should not begin CS courses until they have mathematics equivalent to MATH 1240 Pre-Calculus; it is recommended not to attempt more than 12 credit hours of technical material in one semester. Choice slots (choice:true) represent student selections prescribed by the catalog; their placeholder codes (e.g. SCI-CHOICE-1) are NOT real UNM courses. Context from the catalog's graduation requirements: (4) math sequence MATH 1512, MATH 1522, MATH 314 or 321, STAT 345; (5) 9 communications credits — ENGL 1110, ENGL 1120, plus one of COMM 1130 Public Speaking, ENGL 2120 Intermediate Composition, or ENGL 2210 Professional and Technical Communication; (6) General Education Areas 4-7 plus other non-technical courses to at least 30 credits; (7) four 3+ credit science courses for science/engineering majors, two from one sequence including labs — ASTR 2110/2110L+2115/2115L, BIOL 2110C+2410C, CHEM 1215/1215L+1225/1225L, (ENVS 1130/1130L or GEOL 1110/1110L)+GEOL 2110C, or PHYS 1310/1310L+1320/1320L (physics recommended); (8) a minor outside computer science is required; (3) 51 CS credits incl. 9 technical-elective credits at 300-level or above from CS Department offerings, advisor-approved, grade B or better (at most 3 cr of CS 499; CS 494 excluded). Grades: C- or better for all requirements; C or better (not C-) in the 42 required CS credits; B- or better in MATH 1512 and CS 152L for department admission. Prereq fields are intentionally empty: the catalog's model schedule does not state course-level prerequisites, and per instructions none are invented — consult the catalog/advisor for sequencing.
